primitives.name: Perceptual Spatial Expectation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Perceptual Expectation of Spatial Direction of Goal-Object ONSIDER, first, an experiment illustrating a rat's propensity, before learning and on a basis of immediate stimuli (i.e., perceptually), to select certain spatially directed paths.
primitives.assumptions: Rat behavior is driven by immediate sensory cues; spatial expectation precedes learned behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sensory cues are ambiguous or absent, expectation collapses to uniform distribution.

layer2.mapping: Spatial expectation in rats mirrors Bayesian prior over goal location in GSI; both encode probabilistic directional preference.
layer2.telemetry: Directional struggle intensity relative to goal object position.

primitives.name: Stimulus Dependent Selectivity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Whenever a rat is placed within sight or smell of food, it appears quite obvious, and therefore it tends to remain unremarked, that his selectivities as to surrounding meansobjects are thereby affected.
primitives.assumptions: Selectivity is modulated by sensory availability; behavior is context-sensitive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In absence of stimuli, selectivity becomes random or uniform across alternatives.

layer2.mapping: Stimulus-dependent selectivity underpins GSI's dynamic belief updating mechanism.
layer2.telemetry: Behavioral deviation from baseline in response to food cue.

primitives.name: Goal-Directed Struggle
primitives.verbatim_quote: The rat's strugglings most certainly will tend to be more on the side of the container which is nearer the food.
primitives.assumptions: Struggle direction correlates with proximity to goal; behavior is spatially optimized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When goal is obscured or unreachable, struggle becomes diffuse or non-directional.

layer2.mapping: Struggle direction in rats corresponds to GSE's state transition vector toward goal.
layer2.telemetry: Peak struggle intensity aligned with nearest goal direction.

It operates as a probabilistic map from stimulus space to action space, encoding a prior belief about goal location. This is modeled mathematically as a conditional expectation E[S|I], where S represents spatial direction and I denotes sensory input. The second operator 'stimulus dependent selectivity' modifies this expectation dynamically based on environmental cues, forming a feedback loop. When the stimulus changes—such as moving food—the expectation updates accordingly, reflecting a Bayesian update. The third operator 'goal-directed struggle' quantifies the behavioral manifestation of this expectation, manifesting as a directional force. These primitives form a triadic structure: perception → expectation → action. Failure modes occur when sensory input is degraded or misleading, causing expectation to misalign with reality. The retrocausal genealogy traces back to early work in animal cognition and reinforcement learning, particularly in understanding how animals form spatial expectations without explicit training. The theory of mind considers competing hypotheses: whether the rat's behavior reflects true expectation or mere habituation.
